references.text: Moses and Aaron are called up on the mountain to the Lord, a previous command to go up.
Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu are mentioned as Aaron's sons who were to serve as priests.
Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, who are mentioned here, later died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord.
The seventy elders of Israel are gathered, a parallel to the seventy elders who were called up on the mountain.
Israel's elders are mentioned as leaders of the people, a role they also have in this text.
The people were told to keep their distance from the mountain, corresponding to the command to worship at a distance.
The people stood at a distance while Moses approached the darkness where God was, a similar pattern of worshiping at a distance.
Hebrews refers to the events at Mount Sinai and the awe-inspiring nature of God's presence.
Confirms that the command to go up was carried out by the same people.
